segments.text: Good morning everyone. Before we begin today's lecture on dynamic programming, I have a few quick administrative announcements.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: First, pop quiz on Wednesday covering graph algorithms and breadth-first search.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Second, assignment 3 deadline is next Friday at 11:59 PM. Please submit your solutions on the course portal.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Also remember, the midterm exam will be held on November 12th in the main auditorium.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Now, pay attention to this very important question: what is the difference between optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems?

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: This will come in the exam, so make sure you understand the Bellman-Ford recurrence relation thoroughly.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Does anyone know what the time complexity of the standard memoized Fibonacci sequence is?

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Okay so, you know, as I said basically, dynamic programming allows us to avoid recomputing solved subproblems.

segments.speaker: PROF_TURING
segments.text: Okay so, dynamic programming basically builds solutions from the bottom up.
